tools.name: analyze_headers
tools.description: Check raw HTTP response headers from a deployment you already operate. Returns the same object as POST /v1/analyze. Unknown fields are ignored. A url field is not fetched. Nothing is stored. Nothing is for sale.

tools.name: explain_finding
tools.description: Explain one finding id from the seven. Returns id, severity, why, and answer_page. answer_page is the CSP and clickjacking page for GLC-CSP-MISSING and GLC-FRAME-MISSING, and null for the other five. Unknown fields are ignored. A url field is not fetched. Nothing is stored. Nothing is for sale.

tools.name: get_fix
tools.description: Return the registry snippet for one finding id and one platform. The platforms are caddy, nginx, vercel, netlify, nextjs. tools.name: report_feedback
tools.description: Report one finding id and one outcome. The outcomes are false_positive, fix_worked, fix_failed. The result is id, outcome, and stored false. findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: analyze_headers, get_fix · Private data: get_fix, report_feedback · Public sink: analyze_headers.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: analyze_headers, get_fix · Private data: get_fix, report_feedback · Public sink: analyze_headers

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
